title: Enterprise entitlement options and pricing experiments for isolated (VPC/on-prem) deployments
creator: Ava Martinez
body:
Objective: Design and validate a set of entitlement and pricing experiments for isolated deployments (VPC and on‑prem) that balance predictable revenue, low sales friction, clear upgrade/maintenance expectations, and compliance needs. Scope covers license fee structures, support tiers, upgrade cadences, entitlements transfer rules, and updates to the standard security questionnaire template.

Background: Sales and Solutions Engineering report repeated friction when contracting Private/VPC on‑prem deals: requests for both perpetual and committed models, varied upgrade expectations, and bespoke security questionnaire items that slow procurement. Engineering needs a small set of committed patterns we can support operationally without bespoke work per customer. Legal asks for clearer warranty/upgrade language.

Proposed experiments (3 variants):
1) Capacity Commit (base + commit): base annual platform fee (covers maintenance + monitoring) + committed GPU units tier priced by peak throughput. Includes Standard support and quarterly minor upgrade windows.
2) Term License (tiered flat fee): annual term license by customer size band (small/medium/enterprise) with optional add-on bundles (audit logging, longer retention, on‑prem airgap hotfix channel). Includes Priority support for enterprise band.
3) Hybrid: lower base + per‑token/throughput variable overage plus optional paid accelerated upgrade path and entitlements-transfer credits for M&A scenarios.

Support tiers (draft):
- Standard: 48h business SLA, maintenance windows quarterly, access to community forum, included minor patching.
- Priority: 8h business SLA, scheduled monthly maintenance windows, access to ticketed phone escalation.
- Premium: 2h 24/7 SLA, guaranteed hotfix path for air‑gapped customers with paid overnight deploy option, named Technical Account Manager.

Upgrade cadences and options:
- Minor (security/bug/patch): quarterly by default, unattended for non‑breaking updates.
- Minor+Features: opt‑in monthly feature bundles for Priority/Premium.
- Major: annual; customers can opt into faster major upgrades for a one‑time upgrade credit or subscription add‑on.
- Airgapped/air‑gap hotfix channel: paid channel for emergency security patches with validated offline deployable artifacts.

Operational constraints and engineering asks:
- Need an entitlement ledger in the Control Plane to record license bindings, committed capacity, and upgrade credits.
- Billing integration: map capacity tiers to invoice lines and show line‑item breakdown in Console.
- Clear fallback behaviour if a customer downgrades mid‑term (grace periods, prorations).

Acceptance criteria:
- Draft contract language for each variant in Google Drive (linked).
- 3 pilot customers identified (Sales) and drafted offer emails for pilot enrollment.
- Security questionnaire template updated with standard answers and an FAQ for high‑risk items; Legal signoff recorded.
- Engineering scoped work to implement entitlement ledger and billing flags with estimates and GitHub epics.
- Pricing bands validated by Sales for target ARR and closed‑won threshold.
- Console mockups for licensing UI and billing view (Design feedback captured).

Deliverables:
- Confluence PRD with comparative revenue and engineering cost models.
- Contract templates + SOW snippets.
- Updated security questionnaire and Q&A playbook for Solutions Engineering.
- Internal enablement deck for Sales and AMs.

Risks:
- Overly complex packaging that increases engineering maintenance and sales confusion.
- Security questionnaire answers that exceed our technical guarantees and require additional engineering work.
- Incorrect pricing that cannibalizes Dedicated or Hosted revenue lines.

Next steps:
1) Legal to review draft contract language (ETA 2025-02-25).
2) Pilot offers to 3 customers (Sales) by 2025-03-01.
3) Engineering spike to size entitlement ledger (estimate 4pts) by 2025-03-08.
4) Align on final experiment variants and go/no‑go for pilot by 2025-03-12.
comments: 2025-02-18 | Ava Martinez: Ticket created after scoping sync with Sales and Legal. Captured three initial packaging directions and major asks from Solutions Engineering.
2025-02-20 | Priya Shah (Legal): Reviewed draft contract language; requested explicit warranty and EOL paragraphs for on‑prem MAJOR upgrades. Added TODO in doc: define downgrade/proration flow.
2025-02-24 | Marco Alvarez (Sales): Proposed pilot customers: Acme Health (regulated), FinPivot (mid‑market), and Orion Retail (PLG expansion). Agreed to test both Capacity Commit and Hybrid offers.

2025-02-25 | Nora Liu (Engineering): Confirmed entitlement ledger spike is feasible; raised concern about SKU explosion if we allow too many optional bundles. Recommended canonical feature flags instead of per‑customer SKUs.
2025-03-01 | Design review (Jin Park): Uploaded Console mockups; suggested showing upgrade credits and next billing snapshot prominently to reduce churn risk. See link to Figma in links.
2025-03-03 | Liam O'Connor: Legal signoff pending minor edits. Preparing pilot enrollment emails. Engineering kickoff scheduled for 2025-03-05 to start ledger spike.
2025-03-05 | Ava Martinez: Updated acceptance criteria to include Security Questionnaire signoff and Sales enablement deck. Marked status to In Review so Legal and Sales can comment.
